products.name: Dataiku
products.note: Collaborative data science platform; MLOps; governance workflows; EU-hosted options; GDPR relevant

reading.body:
Dataiku sells a unified platform for enterprise AI that bundles data orchestration, MLOps, and governance workflows, positioning itself as an alternative to fragmented manual processes like spreadsheets and legacy tools.

The platform addresses a real operational constraint in enterprise AI: the gap between data science work and production deployment at scale. Its governance layer, cost controls, and audit capabilities suggest the company believes enterprises will not move data pipelines to AI assistance without visibility and control, particularly under regulatory pressure like GDPR. This matters because compute requirements for AI scale with data volume and pipeline complexity, and enterprises that consolidate scattered tools onto a governed platform may see different resource utilization than those running parallel systems.

The evidence here covers customer adoption in pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, and healthcare, where large organizations have used the platform for specific AI work. Gartner rankings reflect market perception of the platform's scope and execution. These are signals of market position, not of infrastructure, power demand, or the buildings required to serve the platform itself. The data does not show how many organizations use Dataiku, how much compute infrastructure it requires to host, or what fraction of enterprise AI workloads it reaches.

profile_text.body:
Dataiku is a Paris-based company founded in 2013. Its site describes it as the Platform for AI Success, which it says unites people, orchestration, and governance to turn AI investments into measurable business outcomes. The company presents one system for running enterprise AI, with governance applied from the start, unified visibility, cost controls, and audit-ready oversight. It also describes moving analysts off spreadsheets and legacy desktops through AI-assisted, governed pipelines. The platform is tracked as a collaborative data science product in the Data and Analytics AI category, with MLOps, governance workflows, EU-hosted options, and GDPR relevance noted.

The site names several customers. Novartis moved from manual spreadsheet calculations to decision-making with Dataiku and used the Dataiku LLM Mesh for healthcare market research. Johnson & Johnson's Vision team ran a generative AI training and hackathon with Dataiku that produced working prototypes in less than two days. Michelin uses Dataiku across R&D, manufacturing, and services, with the site citing 50+ global manufacturing sites. Dataiku states it has been named a Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for AI Platforms for Data Science and ML for the fifth consecutive year, recognized for both "Completeness of Vision" and "Ability to Execute."

The site also cites a Dataiku/Harris Poll survey of 900 CEOs across eight global markets, in which 80% of CEOs say their role is at risk if their company fails to deliver measurable AI gains by the end of 2026.
